executiveSummary: GM1586's official 2025 identity, contained centre, 30,048 residents, 41 neighbourhoods, seven BAG places, thirteen settlement labels, Lichtenvoorde-Groenlo station and six Dutch NWB border links are internally coherent; neighbourhood population differs by only 33 residents (-0.11%) and is reconciled without rewriting CBS source values. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Official municipal evidence distinguishes extreme-rain road-access problems around the Groenlose Slinge and eastern Lichtenvoorde, and WRIJ describes the Groenlose Slinge/Baakse Beek water-retention and wastewater systems; none supports the canonical major-river case's exact 1.567311 flood-depth field, 14,238 affected resident-equivalents and unchanged T+72 footprint. Pluvial and river maps reuse a common neighbourhood ordering rather than local elevation, drainage and flow paths. A controlled ignition in Buitengebied Vragender ranks its containing neighbourhood only seventeenth of 41, while the canonical wildfire is smoke-only at T+24 and has no source, fuels, wind, peat, access, firewater or suppression state. Static residents omit the Zwarte Cross's officially expected 68,500 visitors per day and other transient exposure. Dutch road, rail and bus geometry does not establish event operation or German-border mutual aid; no acute-care department lies inside the municipality. Exact utilities, supply and recovery outputs are unsupported by physical topology, current operational state or accountable first-72-hour actions. Public observations, restrictions, registers and plans must retain publisher, edition, issue/valid/retrieval time, coverage, licence and evidence class; Unknown and NoData are never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1586 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK/BRT source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1586 as Oost Gelre in Gelderland and reports 30,048 residents, density 273/km2, 25.2% aged 65 or older and 4,033 one-person households. The generated centre [6.572798096955667, 52.00257640046952] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Forty-one neighbourhood rows in seven districts sum to 30,015 residents, 33 below the municipality total (-0.11%); households sum to 12,940 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 7,580. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 30,048 without altering source rows.

BAG supplies seven current woonplaatsen—Groenlo, Harreveld, Lichtenvoorde, Lievelde, Mariënvelde, Vragender and Zieuwent—and BRT supplies thirteen settlement labels: seven woonkernen and six buurtschappen. All place reference points are contained; labels are not occupancy, evacuation or service footprints.

Core population and age fields cover 41/41 neighbourhoods, while housing, tenure, social and access indicators have partial NoData. District heating and public charging cover 0/41. Published zero, null, suppression and not-applicable remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Water- en rioleringsprogramma 2024–2028, climate pages and official 70 mm/hour stress-test interpretation
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal water/climate pages and Water- en rioleringsprogramma 2024–2028; Toekomstverkenning Oost Gelre 2040 stress-test document inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality links a climate atlas for extreme rain, drought and heat, and says its 2024–2028 programme covers collection, transport and processing of wastewater, rainwater, groundwater and municipal surface water. It promotes disconnection, infiltration and buffering at source.

The official future exploration reports that a 70 mm/hour stress test makes major roads in the west and roads around the Groenlose Slinge less passable; eastern Lichtenvoorde can be inaccessible for hours, while western Groenlo access declines but most emergency-service roads remain passable and much rural area remains reachable.

These are official scenario/planning findings, not a current rainfall observation, incident footprint, sewer/pump setting, measured depth, passability state or recovery trajectory. The deployment does not ingest their cell/road footprint.

No standard machine-readable reuse licence, live operational cadence or complete drainage connectivity was identified for the municipal documents/maps; source-specific rights and NoData therefore remain explicit.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Groenlose Slinge, Achterhoek water-retention and Lichtenvoorde wastewater-chain evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current project and water-treatment pages; project research 2024–2025, planning 2026 and anticipated execution 2027; historical RWZI incident update 20 June 2025
supports: WRIJ describes the Groenlose Slinge as a roughly 10 km stream between Winterswijk and Groenlo with a bypass, and is studying changes to retain water during drought while preserving discharge during wet periods. Research/options are not built capacity or current operating state.

The local water chain includes wastewater collection, pumps and pressure mains and RWZI Lichtenvoorde; treatment-system water is discharged toward the Baakse Beek system. Public role/design descriptions do not establish live inflow, storage, controls, backup or restoration.

During the 20 June 2025 silo failure at RWZI Lichtenvoorde, switch cabinets important for control were cleaned, the plant continued operating and some wastewater was diverted. This historical observation demonstrates incident-specific control/diversion decisions, not a default service curve.
The Groenlose Slinge, Baakse Beek, Veengoot and sewer/wastewater mechanisms are distinct from a selected major-river inundation case and from drinking-water supply.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Dated 2026 surface-water and Zwilbroek groundwater abstraction restrictions
evidenceSources.edition: Groundwater restriction issued 10 August 2026 and effective 12 August 2026 08:00; surface-water restriction effective 16 July 2026 12:00; current pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: WRIJ's current page includes Zwilbroek in Oost Gelre among ten vulnerable nature areas subject to a temporary groundwater abstraction ban for irrigation and explains that excessive peat drying can cause irreversible damage.

The same page says a work-area-wide surface-water abstraction ban had applied since 16 July 2026 because of drought. Searches found no later lifting notice by the audit time, but the restriction still requires source refresh and explicit valid/expiry state before operational use.
These are timestamped official operational restrictions, not an ignition, fire perimeter, local soil-moisture raster, municipal drinking-water shortage or unbounded future scenario forcing.
A calendar-bound exercise may attach the restriction only while its confirmed valid interval intersects the scenario; an undated preset must show Unknown rather than silently applying or ignoring it.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 and Dutch-German crisis-cooperation context
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 appendices published March 2025; regional plans and current Dutch-German cooperation pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The regional profile reports 489 hectares of nature in Oost Gelre and assesses nature-fire scenarios alongside flooding, extreme weather, utilities, cyber/telecom and transport disruption. Regional inclusion does not validate municipality-specific intensity, probability or service curves.

VNOG expects longer dry periods to increase the likelihood of larger or less controllable nature fires and uses a region-wide area-oriented nature-fire approach. Nature area is exposure context, not combustible footprint, fuel moisture, current risk phase, ignition or suppression state.

VNOG's policy states its large German border requires coordinated operational execution and refers to arrangements with Kreis Borken and Veiligheidsregio Twente; cooperation covers fire, rescue, ambulance, disaster response and crisis management.

Plans establish responsibilities and possible mutual aid, not incident-time alert, availability, border passage, resource request, arrival, task completion or restoration. No blanket standard redistribution licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Zwarte Cross attendance, camping and traffic-management evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Gemeente Oost Gelre Jaarverslag 2024; 2024 permit decision and 2026 event/traffic notices inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality reports a record 265,500 admissions across the 2024 Zwarte Cross. Its permit decision expected 68,500 visitors per day for the four-day event with festival camping—more than twice the municipality's resident population on an event day.

The 2026 permit again required a mobility plan and fire-safety notification; municipal notices document long build/breakdown periods, local road closures and traffic controls around Besselinkschans in Lichtenvoorde.

Event admission counts are not simultaneous occupancy. A usable scenario needs valid event date, ticket/camping/worker/visitor presence ranges, time of day, entrances/exits, transport mode, medical/shelter resources and road state.
Static CBS residents therefore materially understate potential people present in a Zwarte Cross exercise, while applying festival attendance outside its valid period would also be wrong.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Road, rail and transit graph context for Oost Gelre and the German border
evidenceSources.edition: ProRail Netverklaring 2026; NWB-Light snapshot 1 August 2026 and GTFS/ProRail source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; Gelderland N319 project page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: ProRail lists Lichtenvoorde-Groenlo as a basic station on the Zutphen–Winterswijk railway. The deployment contains that station and forty GTFS stop areas, including Lievelde/Lichtenvoorde and Groenlo, but points/schedules do not establish incident-time operation, passengers, accessibility, capacity or recovery.

The CC0 monthly NWB logical graph has six Dutch cross-boundary links: two N18 series sections toward Berkelland/Oude IJsselstreek and N313, N319 and N312 sections toward Aalten, Berkelland and Winterswijk. Nominal capacities are scenario proxies, not measured emergency throughput.

The graph has no German municipality/road node or jurisdictional border edge. It cannot represent routes and mutual aid toward Kreis Borken/Vreden, while current/project road pages and the graph do not provide a guaranteed emergency detour.
Same physical N18 series sections must not be added as independent capacity; rail/bus/road state requires timestamped operations/restrictions and destination-aware route validation.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / RIVM / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / RWS Waterinfo / NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial public asset, care, grid, communications, education and observation context
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation contains 226 GM1586 points: eight sewer pumps, RWZI Lichtenvoorde and 217 weirs. Capacities exist for eight sewer pumps but not the treatment plant or weirs; connectivity, compatible units, settings, flow, current operation, reserve, backup and restoration remain unavailable.

RIVM contains no acute-care department inside GM1586. Nearest straight-line reference points are Streekziekenhuis Koningin Beatrix in Winterswijk at 9.221 km, Slingeland in Doetinchem at 19.880 km and Gelre Zutphen at 27.736 km. Register role/distance is not travel time, acceptance, staffing, beds or capacity.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Liander area OS DALE 10-1i and reports planning demand/queue/projects with earliest project year 2030. RDI contains 85 antenna installations (35 mobile, 24 fixed-link, seven broadcast, eighteen amateur and one other-mobile) and DUO 23 education records. Planning/register presence is not live topology, load, outage, backhaul, shelter, occupancy or restoration.

No RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast, KNMI weather station or NDW road situation is assigned inside GM1586. Nearest reviewed KNMI observation is Hupsel at 9.249 km and Waterinfo observation Markelo at 22.135 km. Bounded absence is NoData, never normal weather/water or open roads. Dataset licences/cadences differ and remain source-specific.

Administrative centroids and a deterministic seed cannot replace elevation/hydraulic cells, rainfall duration and flow/drainage paths, eligible fuels/peat, source/wind/fire spread, or event-time people and exposed-object geometry.

residualLimitations: No expert-selected WRIJ/LIWO scenario supplies an applicable water boundary level/datum, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival, duration, recession and dewatering for GM1586; the canonical major-river output is unsupported.

The municipal 70 mm/hour conclusions are authoritative scenario evidence, but the deployment lacks their licensed cell/road/building footprint, rainfall duration, surface flow, sewer state, uncertainty and update metadata.

The 226 HWH points lack complete catchment connectivity, flow direction, compatible capacity units, settings, receiving levels, present condition, backup and restoration; surface water, sewer/wastewater and drinking water remain separate.

No public source establishes a current Zwilbroek/Vragender ignition/perimeter, eligible fuel and peat condition, wind/plume, people present, access, extinguishing water, crews or suppression state. The abstraction restriction is dated context only.
The current WRIJ groundwater/surface-water restrictions need a refreshed valid/lifted state for each calendar-bound exercise and cannot silently drive an unbound preset.

Six NWB border links use nominal scenario units and omit Germany, local border roads, cross-border responders, route restrictions and destination-specific emergency throughput; the two N18 segments are series, not additive capacity.
Station and GTFS records do not establish event-time rail/bus operation, passengers, accessibility, disruption or recovery. No integrated local crossing/bridge operational layer was found.

No RIVM acute department lies inside GM1586. Straight-line proximity to SKB/Slingeland and German-border health facilities does not establish ambulance time, border passage, acceptance/diversion, staff, beds, power/oxygen, generator fuel or T+72 throughput.
One Liander planning sample and 85 RDI sites do not establish electricity/gas/telecom topology, coverage, live load, outage, backhaul, backup, reserve, switching or restoration.

CBS residents exclude event visitors/campers/staff, workers, pupils, patients, tourists, cross-border travellers, responders and displaced people; total admissions do not establish simultaneous occupancy or needs.

No in-boundary Waterinfo, KNMI weather or NDW match is a bounded coverage result. External points and missing records remain NoData, never normal conditions, open access or safety; no reviewed local T+48/T+72 forecast exists.

Exact hazard, affected-population, eight-service, recovery and person-hour results remain synthetic exercise outputs, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties or operator commitments until critical/high findings are corrected and reviewed by local and cross-border authorities.

This audit covers the first 72 hours only; water-system recovery, peat/nature restoration, infrastructure repair, displacement, health effects and event/cross-border disruption can last substantially longer.
provinceReviewFlags: Gelderland, Oost Gelre, WRIJ and flood/LIWO experts should define whether a river-flood preset applies locally and, if so, select explicit water boundary, defence/pathway, connected footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData; separately review the 70 mm/hour drainage/road case.

Province, municipality, VNOG/Brandweer, nature managers and German partners should review Zwilbroek/Vragender local peat/nature fire versus external smoke, valid-time drought/readiness, people presence, access, extinguishing water, warnings/closures and suppression state.

Oost Gelre, festival organizers, GHOR/VNOG and transport partners should define privacy-safe, calendar-bound Zwarte Cross population, ingress/egress, medical, shelter, sanitation, water and supply scenarios without treating admissions as occupancy.

Province, Rijkswaterstaat, road authorities, ProRail/operators, OV authorities and Kreis Borken partners should review N18/N319, local German-border routes, Lichtenvoorde-Groenlo rail, bus operation and restriction semantics without treating a schedule or graph edge as live capacity.

Ambulance services, SKB/Slingeland, VNOG and German health/crisis partners should define privacy-safe destination, acceptance/diversion, route alternatives and mutual-aid state; national-register absence is not proof of no cross-border option.

Gelderland, Oost Gelre, WRIJ, utilities and safety partners should adopt one first-72-hour action/resource/evidence contract for warning, water control, evacuation/shelter, access/border, nature fire, care, utilities and resupply, while protecting sensitive topology and keeping Unknown/NoData explicit.
